html:
The Misak, also called Guambiano, are a people of the Andes of Cauca in southwestern Colombia, centred on Silvia, near Popayán. They farm high mountain land and are known for their dress: blue wraps and black skirts or ruanas, with small brimmed hats.

Their land fell under Spanish rule in the 1530s, when Sebastián de Belalcázar founded Popayán. Much of it later became large estates. From the 1970s the Misak and their neighbours the Nasa took back estate lands in a long struggle and rebuilt their councils. In 2020 Misak protesters pulled down a statue of Belalcázar in Popayán, and in 2021 another in Cali.
